neighbours.label: 'come' with an inanimate subject that arrives or appears (a song came on, a call comes in, a test came back, a question came up), as against the same events told with another verb and a person who comes somewhere
fire: We were halfway through dinner when the news came on the television.
Late on Friday an urgent email came in from the head office.
The biopsy came back clear, so the doctors sent her home.
During the interview a tricky question came up about his old job.
Whenever a text comes in, my watch buzzes twice.
Nobody knows exactly how the rumour came about in the first place.
When I ran the numbers again it came out as nearly forty percent.
The old ballad came on just as we reached the coast.
quiet: We were halfway through dinner when the news started on the television.
Late on Friday an urgent email arrived from the head office.
The biopsy was clear, so the doctors sent her home.
During the interview he asked a tricky question about his old job.
Whenever I get a text, my watch buzzes twice.
Nobody knows exactly who started the rumour in the first place.
When I ran the numbers again the total was nearly forty percent.
My uncle came to the coast with us for the weekend.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.8 on came/comes; other verbs and human 'came to dinner' below 0.2
